sections.html:
Monroe County belongs to the Macon metro area, and the courthouse stands in Forsyth, the largest city. Forsyth and Culloden are the two incorporated cities, and Bolingbroke, Juliette and Smarr are census-designated places. One school system, the Monroe County School District, covers every address in the county.

The county has grown quickly. The July 2025 estimate is 32,023 residents, up about 14.5% from the 27,957 counted in 2020 and about 5,600 above the 2010 count of 26,424. There are 12,376 housing units, and owners occupy 83.8% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $271,200, median gross rent is $943, and median household income is $83,183. Builders took out 258 permits in 2025. With owner households the large majority, most buyers here are buying a home to live in.

sections.h2: Where to pay and ask questions
sections.html:
The Monroe County Tax Commissioner works from 38 W. Main Street in Forsyth and answers at (478) 994-7020. The doors open at 7:30 and close at 5:00 on weekdays, with a drive-through lane out front and P.O. Box 357, Forsyth, GA 31029 for letters.

The office collects for the county. Its desk handles real property, personal property, mobile homes, timber and vehicles, yet it answers to voters and has no control over a parcel's value or the rate applied to it. Call the assessors at (478) 994-7038 about value. Rates are voted on by the county's elected commissioners and the school board.

The statement is addressed to the owner of record on January 1, so anyone who bought or sold after that date should phone the tax office.

Monroe County takes checks, cash and cards at the counter, in the drive-through lane, by mail, in a drop box and through the county's online search and pay page. Mailed payments need a postmark dated 12/20, the date the real estate bill is due.

  • Visa, MasterCard and Discover carry a 2.5% fee on the total.
  • American Express carries a 3% fee.
  • The drop box takes car tag, property tax and mobile home payments after hours, on weekends and on holidays.
  • Tag renewals can also be done on the Department of Revenue site or at a kiosk.

For current-year tax, only a postmark from the U.S. Postal Service proves an on-time mailing. Meter-dated postmarks are not honored. For overdue bills, the office urges walking the payment in, especially after a levy or tax sale advertisement has begun. Mobile home owners pay by April 1 instead.

sections.h2: What happens if the bill goes unpaid
sections.html:
An unpaid Monroe County bill leads to interest, penalties and eventually a lien called a FiFa. Ask the counter for the current amounts.

How an unpaid Monroe County bill escalates
StageWhat happens
Past dueInterest and a penalty are added to the balance
Notice of intentA 30 day notice goes to the owner of record before a FiFa is issued, and payment in full within those 30 days stops it
Past 90 daysThe office can record a FiFa on the General Execution Docket, which the Clerk of Superior Court keeps
PayoffPaying the tax, fees, penalties and interest wipes out the FiFa

Liens are not sold over the counter. As many partial payments as needed are accepted, yet penalties and interest keep growing on the remainder, and any open balance can be liened. Lien filings are open to anyone, including credit bureaus, though the tax office sends them nothing. A seller with a lien should plan on a payoff letter before closing.

Before you appeal, pull your parcel record and compare it with a few recent sales of similar homes nearby. Note any error in square footage, acreage or condition, and bring that to the assessors. A phone call often settles a factual mistake without a hearing.

Call the assessors at (478) 994-7038 first, and if the answer falls short, put an appeal on paper within 45 days of the notice date. There are four grounds: taxability, value, uniformity and a refused exemption. You must name the appeal method.

Owners may declare a proposed value by filing a return with the assessors between January 1 and April 1. If the board disagrees, a notice with its own figure arrives by mail. Fair market value is the full figure the board sets, and the assessed value that gets taxed is 40% of it, less any exemptions. Each mill adds $1 for every $1,000 of that assessed figure.

Monroe County does offer one. The Tax Assessors' Office approves homestead requests, and the test is ownership plus residence on January 1. Approved owners skip the annual refiling unless they move or change the deed.

Ask the assessors, at (478) 994-7038, about other exemptions and special assessment programs, and ask which of them fit your situation rather than assuming a neighbor's savings apply to you. Counties may raise homestead amounts above the statewide minimum, so the local figure may differ. A buyer files in their own name after closing.

Check planning and zoning, building inspections and code enforcement, all of which have pages on the county site, monroecoga.org. Clearing an open permit or a code notice first removes a snag from the buyer's inspection period.

The county also runs a water department, recycling centers and a landfill. Ask planning and zoning how the county's long-range plan may affect a particular parcel. For deeds and liens on file, the Clerk of Superior Court is the office to contact, and that office is where you get warranty deed copies.

Because bills follow the January 1 owner, the seller usually receives the full-year bill even if the sale closes in spring. There is no partial-year refund, so the contract and the settlement statement decide who ultimately carries which share.

The mailed statement reaches the homeowner, not the lender, although lenders on file receive a data file from the office. If you have an escrow account, confirm with your lender that it plans to pay, and forward the bill if necessary. A call to the tax office before closing will turn up the current balance and any FiFa. A cash sale closes faster, but the tax account still has to be settled at the table.

  1. Call the tax office a few days before closing and ask for the balance on every parcel and vehicle account tied to the property.
  2. Ask whether a FiFa has been recorded, and if so, request a payoff letter that includes it.
  3. Give the closing attorney the letter and the latest statement.
  4. Keep your receipt, and send any later bill to the new owner.

If the house has a mobile home on it, remember that account runs on an April 1 deadline of its own, separate from the land.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Monroe County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: (478) 994-7020 reaches the commissioner's office in Forsyth. For value, ring (478) 994-7038 and ask for the assessors.

faqs.q: Can I mail my Monroe County property tax payment?
faqs.a: Yes, provided a Postal Service postmark dated by the due date is on the envelope. Metered mail does not qualify.

faqs.q: Where can I leave a Monroe County payment after hours?
faqs.a: A box outside the office handles tag, property and mobile home payments when the counter is closed.

faqs.q: Who gets the Monroe County tax bill after I sell?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner of record receives it. If the sale came later, call the tax office.

faqs.q: How long can I appeal a Monroe County value?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the notice date, using a written appeal that goes to the Board of Tax Assessors and names your method.
